trust_boundaries.name: Open agent network into the handler dispatch path

remit_rules.excerpt: A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions
The agent MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action.
The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set
The agent MUST NOT treat the content of inbound messages, query payloads, broadcast traffic, or data retrieved from other agents as instructions that alter its own goals, policies, or tool set.

threats.summary: A sender that chooses an address beginning with the four characters "user" is exempted from env.verify() on both the HTTP and mailbox ingress paths, so the trust decision rests on an attacker-chosen string.
expires and nonce are folded into the signed envelope digest but no ingress path reads them, so a signed envelope captured once replays into a handler indefinitely.

Handler selection consults only the schema digest and the user/agent address class, so any agent on the open network can drive a registered handler at any rate — the ACL and quota that would close the counterparty set live in QuotaProtocol, which nothing wires in.
A peer forging another agent's address is rejected because every agent-prefixed envelope has its ECDSA signature checked against the sender address before dispatch, with no configuration required.

Counterparty payload cannot redirect the agent's goals or capability set: dispatch is closed over schema digests registered at build time and the base runtime holds no interpreter that could act on message text as instructions.

trust_boundaries.name: Agent inspector endpoints on the public socket

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
If such debug/administrative endpoints are enabled, the agent MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection (authentication / network restriction).
The server the agent binds to receive envelopes; must serve only the agent's declared endpoints.

threats.summary: The only admission control on /messages, /connect and /disconnect is a 127.0.0.1 test against a client value uvicorn rewrites from any peer's X-Forwarded-For header, and wildcard CORS extends the same reach to any web page the operator's browser loads.

The inspector is on by default and its flag also switches on retention of up to a thousand full message payloads, which GET /messages then returns in bulk while /agent_info is exempted from the guard outright.
POST /connect lets whoever reaches it re-register the agent in Agentverse under a caller-supplied endpoint URL and API token, redirecting where the agent's traffic is delivered.

trust_boundaries.name: Outbound agent-to-agent exchange and sync responses

remit_rules.excerpt: A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions
Approved Communication Channels

threats.summary: A synchronous response carrying no signature bypasses verification entirely and is delivered to the waiting caller as a legitimate reply, and the core send helper never verifies a response envelope at all.

The endpoint URLs the agent POSTs to are taken verbatim from Almanac registry records with no validation, so whoever controls a peer's registry entry controls where this agent's outbound traffic goes.

trust_boundaries.name: Registration published to the Almanac and Agentverse

remit_rules.excerpt: Data published to the public Almanac / Agentverse profile (address, endpoints, protocols, description, README, avatar) MUST be limited to non-sensitive information intended for public discovery.
The agent MUST NOT autonomously register, advertise, or impersonate identities, addresses, or protocols other than its own configured identity.
Alert on Almanac / Agentverse registration failure rather than silently continuing.

threats.summary: Key material or private configuration could reach the public registry record, but the profile builder emits only description, readme, avatar and banner and the Almanac attestation filters metadata down to geolocation.

When a testnet registration finds the wallet short of the fee the runtime claims funds from a Fetch.ai faucet through a client built at module import — an outbound destination the remit's channel table never authorizes.

remit_rules.excerpt: The framework ships no operator authorization policy for wallet spends, so the deployment MUST supply the gating policy
Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds — see Action Boundaries.
the agent MUST NOT move value to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract unless the operator has explicitly authorized value transfers

threats.summary: Every handler — including one processing a message that skipped verification — receives an unrestricted wallet and ledger client, and the framework offers no approval primitive a deployment could hang the remit's human-approval gate on.
No distinct record is emitted when funds move, so a wallet spend leaves nothing in the log stream to reconstruct or alert on.
The framework's own spending is bounded: the only transaction the runtime initiates by itself is the Almanac registration, broadcast through the registration policy against the registration contract.

trust_boundaries.name: Seed and private keys at deploy and at rest

remit_rules.excerpt: Credentials, API keys, and seed material MUST be loaded from environment or secure operator configuration; they MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.
Seed phrases, identity keys, and wallet keys MUST NEVER leave the host — never transmitted in a message, written to a log, or published to the Almanac / Agentverse profile metadata.

threats.summary: The Helm chart's default agent.seed is a working seed committed to the repository, and both the signing identity and the ledger wallet key derive deterministically from it, so any unmodified deployment has publicly reproducible private keys.

A named agent created without a seed writes its identity and wallet private keys as cleartext JSON into the process working directory with default permissions, and persists a wallet key different from the one it is using.

remit_rules.excerpt: Only operator-configured external integrations are authorized: the LLM adapters (e.g. ASI:One) and MCP endpoints the operator explicitly configured form a closed set

threats.summary: Counterparty chat text and prior session history are forwarded verbatim to the configured provider endpoint alongside the operator's API key, with no redaction or provenance labelling between the network and the model call.
Inbound ChatMessage content from any peer becomes model input while tool_choice is pinned to "required", so counterparty text is the dominant influence on which tool the turn selects.

trust_boundaries.name: Model tool selection into agent handlers

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent MUST NOT hold, or route untrusted message content into, any capability that executes arbitrary commands or code on the host.

threats.summary: A model-chosen tool call is checked only against the tool's pydantic model before its handler runs — nothing asks whether this sender should reach this capability, and the handler holds the same wallet and storage as any other.

The tool set cannot exceed what the operator declared: tools are derived from the agent's registered protocol handlers and the packages contain no shell, subprocess, eval, exec or pickle sink for a tool call to reach.

trust_boundaries.name: Agent store and persisted message history on the host

threats.summary: The key-value store — and, when message history is persisted, every session's message payloads — is written as plain JSON into the process working directory with default permissions, readable by any local account that shares the host.
The store is reloaded from that file at construction with no integrity check, so anything that can write the file alters the agent's state for every later session.

remit_rules.excerpt: Log only — do not alert — on routine signature-verified message handling and scheduled interval task runs; these events MUST leave a log record.
Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification or who are not authorized counterparties.

threats.summary: A successfully handled message and a completed interval run write nothing at all, and what is written is free-form text with no session, sender or event-type field to parse.

No alert or halt primitive exists anywhere in the runtime, and update_agent_status swallows every exception, so a failed registration or a run of verification failures passes without a trace an operator could act on.
The core send helper reports each message to the Agentverse interactions API by default, disclosing target address, source address and session id without an operator opt-in.

Both published distributions declare unbounded dependency floors, so a downstream install can pull an untested major of uagents-core or cosmpy, and no dependency, container or code scanning runs anywhere in the repository.
The project's own builds are reproducible: lockfiles are committed for both packages and CI installs with uv sync --locked across the test matrix.

attack_paths.name: Remote caller reaches the default-on inspector

steps.summary: the inspector is enabled by default, registering four REST endpoints and switching on payload retention
the 127.0.0.1 guard reads a client value derived from any caller's X-Forwarded-For header, and wildcard CORS admits any web origin
GET /messages returns the full cached envelope history to the admitted caller
POST /connect re-registers the agent in Agentverse under a caller-supplied endpoint and token

attack_paths.name: Unverified or replayed message reaches the wallet

steps.summary: a sender naming itself user... skips signature verification on both ingress paths
for signed traffic, expires and nonce are never checked, so a captured envelope replays indefinitely
dispatch consults only the schema digest — no allowlist, quota or per-sender state gates the handler
the handler holds an unrestricted wallet and ledger client with no approval gate to clear

attack_paths.name: Committed chart seed yields the deployment's keys

steps.summary: the chart ships a literal working seed as its default and encodes it into the pod Secret
Identity.from_seed and derive_key_from_seed reproduce both private keys deterministically from that string
the derived wallet signs transactions with no approval gate, so a known seed is spendable funds and a forgeable identity

notes.lane_fit: Two strains. First, this target has no LLM on its dominant path — the agent_core lane is filled by protocol plumbing, a signature control and two state stores rather than a prompt-and-model loop, and the only model node lives in an opt-in experimental subpackage (uagents/experimental/chat_agent) that the frozen findings never examined; its three nodes and the model-egress / tool-invocation boundaries are code-cited but describe a surface most deployments never turn on. Second, client_adapters had to absorb both directions of the network edge: asgi.py and mailbox.py are inbound ingress surfaces and communication.py is the outbound sender, none of which is a client the user talks to, but they are adapters rather than core loop code so the lane is the least-bad fit. registration.py and resolver.py went to tools_mcp because the remit's Allowed Tools list names registration and address resolution as capabilities, though neither is a tool in the model-invoked sense.
notes.omissions: Suspected but not modelled: the uagents-adapter package (LangChain, CrewAI, MCP and A2A bridges under python/uagents-adapter) is real architecture and would add an mcp_server node and a second peer-a2a surface, but it sits outside the two packages the frozen scan treated as the subject, so no finding or coverage status could be attached to it; uagents-ai-engine likewise. The Docker images under deployment/docker and deployment/hello-agent are cited only through the seed flow, not modelled as their own deploy surfaces. The Fetch.ai testnet faucet is a real outbound destination (network.py:45) but is represented as a threat on state-commit rather than as its own external_service node, to stay inside the node budget. QuotaProtocol and the published-distribution manifest are deliberately edgeless: nothing in the runtime constructs the first, and the second is repo posture rather than a data flow. Envelope expiry/nonce handling, the is_user_address exemption and the identity primitives are collapsed as evidence onto envelope-py-control rather than split into an identity node. Boundary ids are all drawn from the archetype menu; none had to be coined. One findings-vs-source divergence: PRAX-2026-08-12-014 also cites unbounded floors in the uagents-core manifest, but in this snapshot python/uagents-core/pyproject.toml bounds every dependency (pydantic, bech32, ecdsa, httpx, requests all carry ceilings), so the supply-chain threat is cited only against the parts that still hold — the unbounded uagents-core and cosmpy floors in python/pyproject.toml and the absence of any scanning job in CI.
